entries.name: Hungarian
entries.definition: A Uralic language, the official language of Hungary.

entries.name: Hup
entries.definition: An Amazonian language spoken by the Hupda people along the border of Brazil and Colombia.

entries.name: Igbo
entries.definition: A Niger-Congo language spoken mainly by the Igbo people of southeastern Nigeria.

entries.name: Indonesian
entries.definition: A standardized form of Malay, the national language of Indonesia.

entries.name: Italian
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken mainly in Italy and Switzerland.

entries.name: J#
entries.definition: A Microsoft programming language with Java-language syntax for the .NET Framework, now discontinued.

entries.name: Japanese
entries.definition: The language of Japan, written with kanji and kana.

entries.name: Java
entries.definition: Writing programs in Java.

entries.name: JavaScript
entries.definition: Writing programs in JavaScript.

entries.name: JDOQL
entries.definition: The object query language of Java Data Objects (JDO), used to retrieve persistent Java objects with filter expressions written in Java-like syntax.

entries.name: JHDL
entries.definition: A hardware description language, developed at Brigham Young University, in which circuits are described with Java classes.

entries.name: Jiba
entries.definition: A Jukunoid language spoken in Nigeria.

entries.name: JScript
entries.definition: Microsoft's implementation of the ECMAScript language, used in Internet Explorer and Windows Script Host.

entries.name: JScript .NET
entries.definition: A version of Microsoft's JScript language that compiles to .NET code and adds features such as typed variables and classes.

entries.name: Julia
entries.definition: A high-level, dynamic programming language designed for fast numerical and scientific computing.

entries.name: Kachin
entries.definition: A Tibeto-Burman language spoken by the Kachin people of northern Myanmar and neighbouring parts of China and India.

entries.name: Kalenjin
entries.definition: A Nilotic language, or cluster of closely related languages, spoken by the Kalenjin people of Kenya.

entries.name: Kannada
entries.definition: A Dravidian language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Karnataka.

entries.name: Kazakh
entries.definition: A Turkic language, the official language of Kazakhstan.

entries.name: Keyhole Markup Language
entries.definition: An XML-based markup language for describing geographic features, placemarks and map views, used by Google Earth and other mapping software.

entries.name: Khmer
entries.definition: The Austroasiatic language of Cambodia, written in the Khmer script.

entries.name: Kinyarwanda
entries.definition: A Bantu language, the national language of Rwanda.

entries.name: Kirundi
entries.definition: A Bantu language, the national language of Burundi.

entries.name: Kokborok
entries.definition: A Tibeto-Burman language spoken mainly in Tripura, India, and in Bangladesh, also called Tripuri.

entries.name: Korean
entries.definition: The language of Korea, written in the Hangul script and spoken in North and South Korea.

entries.name: Korwa
entries.definition: An Austroasiatic language of the Munda branch spoken by the Korwa people of central-eastern India.

entries.name: Kotlin
entries.definition: A statically typed programming language from JetBrains that runs on the Java Virtual Machine and is widely used for Android apps.

entries.name: Kurdish
entries.definition: A group of Northwestern Iranian languages and dialects spoken by Kurds in Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.

entries.name: Kurukh
entries.definition: A Dravidian language spoken by the Oraon people of eastern India and neighbouring parts of Nepal and Bangladesh.

entries.name: Kyrgyz
entries.definition: A Turkic language, the official language of Kyrgyzstan.

entries.name: Ladder logic
entries.definition: A graphical programming language for programmable logic controllers, resembling electrical relay-logic diagrams.

entries.name: Ladino
entries.definition: The Romance language descended from medieval Spanish that is spoken by Sephardic Jewish communities.

entries.name: Lango
entries.definition: A Nilotic language spoken by the Lango people of northern Uganda.

entries.name: Lao
entries.definition: A Kra-Dai language, the official language of Laos.

entries.name: Lawa
entries.definition: An Austroasiatic language of the Palaungic branch spoken by the Lawa people of northern Thailand.

entries.name: LESS
entries.definition: A CSS preprocessor language that adds variables, nesting, mixins and functions to style sheets and compiles to plain CSS.

entries.name: Lingala
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken along the Congo River and widely used as a lingua franca in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo.

entries.name: Lingo
entries.definition: The scripting language of Macromedia Director, later Adobe Director, used to build multimedia and games.

entries.name: Liquid template language
entries.definition: An open-source template language, created by Shopify, that uses objects, tags and filters to build dynamic web pages.

entries.name: Lisp
entries.definition: A family of programming languages originating in 1958, built on parenthesized prefix notation and linked-list data.
